title: Keeling Curve begins at Mauna Loa
summary: In March 1958 Charles David Keeling of Scripps began measuring atmospheric carbon dioxide at the NOAA weather station on Mauna Loa, Hawaii, using an infrared gas analyzer bought with International Geophysical Year funds. The first day's reading was 313 ppm. NOAA calls the Mauna Loa data the longest record of direct atmospheric CO2 measurements; NOAA started its own parallel series in May 1974.

uncertainty.note: The record is continuing; the pin dates its start.
